articles.body: An Egyptian court has sentenced 12 people, including television presenter Sarah Khalifa, to death after convicting them on drug charges.They were part of a “criminal gang” that imported ingredients used to manufacture drugs for sale. They were also found in possession of illegal firearms and ammunition, BBC reported citing state-owned Al-Ahram newspaper.Although the verdict was announced last month, it was only confirmed now after the court obtained a religious opinion from Egypt's grand mufti, fulfilling a legal requirement in death cases.The verdict is subject to appeal.The trialDuring the trial, the court heard that authorities had seized more than 750kg (1,653lbs) of narcotics, along with raw materials imported to manufacture them.Twenty witnesses gave statements to prosecutors, while electronic evidence included conversations and video clips.The defendants were convicted of drug trafficking and rape — “crimes that did not amount to ‘intentional killing’ to which the use of the death penalty must be restricted under international law and standards.”Who is Sarah KhalifaThe 39-year-old presenter, who has denied the charges, is best known for her television programme Mission Impossible, which focused on crime-related issues.During a court hearing in September last year, Khalifa was questioned by the judge about her alleged involvement in the case. articles.title: Scientists discover nearly 1 billion tons of water locked inside Utah's rocky glaciers, using gravity measurements to map ice buried beneath mountain debris
articles.summary: US News: At first glance, Utah's rocky mountain slopes may look completely dry, with loose stones and boulders covering the ground. But beneath some of those r.
articles.body: At first glance, Utah's rocky mountain slopes may look completely dry, with loose stones and boulders covering the ground. But beneath some of those rocks lies an enormous store of frozen water. Researchers have now estimated that Utah's rock glaciers contain about 0.99 gigatonnes, or nearly 1 billion tons, of water equivalent. These unusual formations are bodies of ice buried beneath thick layers of rock and debris, allowing them to survive in places where conventional glaciers cannot. The discovery comes from a study of the Timpanogos Rock Glacier beneath Mount Timpanogos, where scientists used subtle changes in Earth's gravitational field to reconstruct what was hidden underground. Published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Earth Surface, the research was led by Bronson Cvijanovich with Michael S. Thorne, Surya Pachhai, Leif S. Anderson, Ivan Tochimani-Hernandez, Christian L. Hardwick and Tonie van Dam, from the University of Utah and Utah Geological Survey.A glacier hidden beneath rocksRock glaciers look nothing like the bright, exposed ice fields people normally associate with glaciers. They are instead masses of ice covered by layers of loose rocks and debris, with the ice slowly moving downhill beneath the surface. That rocky blanket can insulate the ice from warmth and sunlight, allowing these formations to persist in mountain environments that may no longer support conventional glaciers. The researchers explain in their study, ‘The Internal Ice Content of Timpanogos Rock Glacier, Utah, USA From 3-D Bayesian Inversion of Gravity Data,’ that rock glaciers are increasingly important as climate change reduces conventional glacier ice. They can store water, provide refuges for cold-adapted species and, if destabilised, create hazards for communities below. Yet scientists have struggled to determine exactly how much ice these formations contain because their rocky surfaces hide their interiors.Scientists used gravity to see underground iceTo look beneath Timpanogos Rock Glacier, the team turned to a method that does not require drilling through the entire formation. They collected 232 gravity measurements across the site and used a three-dimensional Bayesian inversion to reconstruct the hidden structure. Ice is substantially less dense than the surrounding bedrock, so a sufficiently large buried ice mass creates a tiny but measurable reduction in gravitational acceleration. By mapping these variations, researchers could estimate where the ice-rich material was located and how thick it was. The study also found an estimated ice volume of about 1.55 million cubic metres, with an average thickness of 18.8 metres. The researchers' preferred model indicates that the entire rock glacier is about 72% ice by volume, while its ice core is approximately 83% ice.One Utah rock glacier holds hundreds of swimming pools of waterThe amount of ice beneath Mount Timpanogos is difficult to visualise, so the researchers compared it with something more familiar. Their estimated 1.55 million cubic metres of ice is roughly equivalent to the volume of 600 Olympic-sized swimming pools. More importantly, Timpanogos Rock Glacier provided the researchers with a way to estimate the hidden water stored across many similar formations. Using their measurements alongside data from other rock glaciers, the team developed a new area-volume relationship. In the research this method produced an estimate of 0.99 gigatonnes of water equivalent for Utah's intact rock glaciers. The western United States was estimated to contain about 11.92 gigatonnes, while intact rock glaciers worldwide could hold approximately 48.03 gigatonnes.A hidden water reserve facing a changing climateThe discovery matters because rock glaciers could become increasingly important as conventional glaciers retreat. Their insulating debris can protect buried ice for longer, making them relatively resilient stores of frozen water in warming mountain environments. But the researchers also caution that their estimates are not perfectly complete. Persistent snow and steep terrain prevented gravity measurements in the upper reaches of Timpanogos Rock Glacier, meaning the calculated ice volume is likely a lower estimate of the total. The study also notes uncertainties in modelling the relationship between ice thickness and density. Even so, the findings reveal a substantial reservoir that is almost invisible from the surface. As temperatures rise and mountain ice changes, understanding these buried stores could become increasingly important for water resources, ecosystems and assessing hazards in alpine regions.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Former US President Joe Biden's son Hunter Biden has suggested that he "may have to" run for president in 2028, citing his commitment to the rule of law as his top qualification for the job.In an upcoming interview with radio host John Catsimatidis, Hunter said he could consider a presidential bid if he received Catsimatidis' endorsement."If I get your endorsement, I may have to (run for president)," Hunter said, adding that one of his biggest concerns was the "50 million Americans that are still suffering with their addictions."Asked about his qualifications for the presidency, Hunter pointed to his commitment to the US Constitution and the rule of law."Here is my qualification for becoming president: if you believe in the Constitution of the United States of America that you swear to uphold and protect. I want the next president to commit to one thing: to adhering to the rule of law," he said.However, Hunter stopped short of committing to a presidential run, saying Democrats have an "incredible bench.""I love Gavin Newsom, personally," he said.Hunter had also joked about entering politics and running for president in 2028 in June.During an upcoming episode of California Governor Gavin Newsom's programme, "This Is Gavin Newsom", Newsom playfully introduced Hunter as "Presidential candidate Hunter Biden."A presidential run would mark Hunter Biden's first entry into the country's political leadership after his earlier career in the US Navy ended in 2014 following a positive cocaine test at the age of 44.The Delaware-born artist has previously been at the centre of political controversy over material from his laptop, which was published by The Post and included allegations that he had used his father's position as vice president to benefit his family.The laptop also contained explicit photographs and material related to drug use and was cited as evidence in Hunter's federal gun and tax cases.On December 1, 2024, President Joe Biden issued a full and unconditional pardon to his son, covering all offences committed between 2014 and 2024. articles.title: Krakatau volcano erupts in Indonesia: 209 flights hit, schools shut as ash plume soars 50,000 feet
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Indonesia suspended hundreds of flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Sunday after Mount Anak Krakatau erupted, sending volcani.
articles.body: Indonesia suspended hundreds of flights at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Sunday after Mount Anak Krakatau erupted, sending volcanic ash across parts of western Indonesia.The disruption affected 209 flights, including several international services, according to Indonesia’s transportation ministry.Indonesia’s Geological Agency said the volcano, located in the Sunda Strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra, had shown increased activity on Saturday before erupting for about 30 seconds at 3:53am on Sunday.“Due to increased activity from the Mount Anak Krakatau eruption, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has temporarily suspended flight operations from 5:30 am to 9.30 am,” the airport said in an early Sunday travel advisory.The suspension was later extended from an earlier scheduled reopening at 5:30am because of volcanic ash, the transportation ministry said. Passengers at the country’s busiest airport sought refunds and reclaimed checked baggage as cancellation notices appeared on departure boards, according to AP.Indonesia’s Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said volcanic ash had spread across parts of Jakarta and Lampung province on the southern tip of Sumatra.The meteorological agency BMKG said satellite observations showed ash reaching 20,000 feet (6,000 metres) on the Java side of the volcano, while another plume rose as high as 50,000 feet (15,000 metres) on the Sumatra side and over parts of Banten province.Two ash clouds were identified using satellite imagery. One plume was moving northeast, affecting areas including Jakarta, Banten and West Java, while the second was moving west and northwest over Lampung, Bengkulu, the southern Sunda Strait and parts of the Indian Ocean west of Sumatra.There were no reports of casualties and no evacuation order was issued. The nearest settlement is more than 16 kilometres from the volcano. Authorities, however, warned residents and visitors to remain at least 3 kilometres from the active crater.Indonesia’s disaster mitigation agency, BNPB, “urges the public to remain calm while increasing vigilance.” Spokesperson Berton Panjaitan also told Reuters that people should wear masks and eye protection during ashfall, reduce outdoor activity, cover water sources and take care while driving because volcanic ash can reduce visibility.Several schools cancelled activities on Saturday after students and residents reported eye irritation, while fishermen suspended trips, local media outlet Kompas reported.Authorities said there was no imminent tsunami risk. Anak Krakatau’s 2018 eruption caused a tsunami that killed at least 430 people on Java and Sumatra.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Rescuers in southeastern China's Jiangxi province found one of the people missing after a mudslide triggered by torrential rain from tropical cyclone Saudel, state broadcaster CCTV reported Sunday.However, the person was found dead, bringing the death toll to two and leaving 10 people still missing.The mudslide struck a village in Suichuan County, Jiangxi province, early Saturday, prompting rescuers to evacuate residents to safer areas, authorities said.One person pulled from the debris was found dead, while two others were rescued alive and in good condition.Typhoon Saudel made two landfalls in Zhejiang province on August 28 before making a third as a tropical storm in neighbouring Fujian province on Thursday, China's official Xinhua news agency reported.In Fujian, several people remained unaccounted for after days of heavy rain, while more than 100 houses collapsed in Huating Town in Putian city, Xinhua reported. articles.summary: Tech News News: The New York City Council is reportedly gearing up for a hearing centered on the use of a hidden, encrypted messaging channel by the administration of.
articles.body: The New York City Council is reportedly gearing up for a hearing centered on the use of a hidden, encrypted messaging channel by the administration of NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani to feed favourable coverage to close to 200 social media influencers. According to a report by The New York Post, Manhattan lawmaker Gale Brewer, who chairs the council's Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation, has said that the hearing has been set for September 22.Alongside this, Queens Councilman Phil Wong is expected to introduce a separate bill demanding greater transparency from City Hall regarding this practice. The bill would require influencers working alongside city agencies on messaging campaigns to clearly disclose their posts and videos with a label such as “Paid for by NYC.”‘City Hall officials collaborated with 189 influencers’Mayor Mamdani’s use of influencers to amplify his administration's messaging first came to light this week through a detailed report published by the Columbia Journalism Review. The report claims that the officials in the City Hall had been in regular contact with 189 social media influencers through a Signal group chat titled “NYC Creators Announcements.” Within this chat, officials reportedly shared daily updates, talking points and video clips that influencers could then use in their own content.The report also revealed that some of these influencers were compensated through formal contracts with city agencies specifically for their involvement in certain messaging campaigns. Others, however, said they participated simply because they supported Mamdani's agenda and found that the coverage helped grow their own follower base.The report says that it remains unclear whether the Signal chat was configured to auto-delete messages, a setting that, if used, would potentially violate the city's official record-keeping laws.What proposed bill will aimsWong’s proposed bill aims specifically to expose any payments made to digital creators that may currently be hidden from public view, particularly in cases where they were brought on as subcontractors.“New Yorkers don't want their tax dollars going to grifting influencers from out of state who are paid to tell us everything here is great when we know damn well it isn't,” Wong said, adding, “If City Hall has to pay people who don't even live here to sell New Yorkers on how wonderful New York is, that tells you everything you need to know.”However, multiple insiders told The publication that holding the Mamdani administration accountable for its use of unpaid influencers offering glowing coverage may prove considerably more complicated.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: 'Highly useful' but no breakthrough: What was discussed in Putin-US talks on Ukraine
articles.summary: US News: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s three-hour meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow ended without any reported breakthrough.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s three-hour meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow ended without any reported breakthrough on a Ukraine peace deal, even as the Kremlin described the talks as “highly useful” and said discussions would continue.Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the meeting, which lasted three hours and 10 minutes, was substantive, constructive and extremely frank and took place in a trusting atmosphere, according to Russia’s TASS news agency.What was discussed?The US envoys “outlined a number of ideas regarding possible avenues for a settlement”, Ushakov said. He did not disclose the details of those proposals, leaving unclear whether they addressed the most contentious issues between Moscow and Kyiv, including territory and the future security arrangements for Ukraine.Ushakov said Putin presented Moscow’s assessment of the war and stressed Russia’s battlefield gains.“In particular, note was taken of the real advances made by the Russian army within the combat zone; confidence was expressed in achieving the stated objectives, and the need to eliminate all root causes of the conflict was emphasised,” he said, according to ANI.Putin also reiterated Moscow’s willingness to pursue political and diplomatic solutions with Washington. The Kremlin has repeatedly said any settlement must address what it calls the “root causes” of the conflict.The discussions also moved beyond the war. “The talks went beyond a mere exchange of views on resolving the Ukrainian crisis. Economic issues and potential major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects were discussed in some detail,” Ushakov said, according to Reuters.“Overall, one can say that the negotiations were timely and highly useful for both sides,” he added.Putin also praised US President Donald Trump’s efforts to end the war.“Understanding that he is entering a difficult situation, he nevertheless does not stop his efforts to help bring about a settlement and to make his contribution to resolving the Russian-Ukrainian conflict,” Putin said in a televised remarks at the start of the talks..A White House official told Reuters the talks were “substantive” and that next steps would be announced in the coming weeks.The US envoys were due to travel to Kyiv on Sunday for talks with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Ushakov said they would convey Putin’s observations on prospects for a “durable peaceful settlement”, while Moscow and Washington would maintain further contact through the envoys.Despite the positive language from Moscow, the central disputes remain unresolved, leaving the next round of US contacts with Kyiv crucial to determining whether the latest diplomatic push can narrow the gap between the two sides.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Sunday backed students protesting against alleged irregularities in Maharashtra Public Servi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Sunday backed students protesting against alleged irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations, saying that "every student is tormented by the BJP regime".In a post on X, Rahul said thousands of students were protesting in Maharashtra because their trust in the system had been "shattered"."In Maharashtra, thousands of students are on the streets, protesting peacefully - the reason isn't just one exam or recruitment, but a trust that's been shattered by the entire system," Rahul said."Whether it's the central or state government, every student is tormented by the BJP regime. Paper leaks, stalled recruitments, the unbearable cost of education, inhumane conditions in hostels, food like poison, fraud in DBT and now, they've seized control of a constitutional body like MPSC and destroyed its credibility," he added.The Congress leader urged the government to listen to the students and act immediately, warning that their protests would grow louder until justice was served."Every demand from students for their successful future is justified. The government must listen to their voice and act immediately - otherwise, this echo of the students will only grow louder until justice is served," Rahul said.Rahul's remarks came amid an ongoing Mumbai Police probe into the alleged leak of the question paper for the MPSC Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Inspector examination.MPSC conducted the offline examination for Drug Inspector posts on March 22. Candidates had subsequently raised concerns over a possible paper leak, but alleged that their complaints were not acted upon. The recruitment process was later completed, with a merit list of 488 candidates published.MPSC has since cancelled the recruitment process for Drug Inspector Group-B posts under the Food and Drug Administration Department following a preliminary inquiry into alleged malpractice in the screening examination.A police inquiry prima facie indicated that one candidate had received the question paper before the examination and benefited from it, the commission said. It added that it considered the seriousness of the findings before deciding to cancel the recruitment process.Police have also arrested six people, including three MPSC officials, in connection with the alleged question paper leak in the 2026 Drug Inspector Group-B screening examination, which has now been cancelled.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: UK weather: Summer-like warmth to make brief return as temperatures near 28C
articles.summary: A summer-like day is in store for some on Sunday with above average temperatures, but the heat will be short-lived.
articles.body:
Temperatures could touch 28C (82F) in parts of the UK on Sunday as summer-like warmth makes a brief return.

A southerly wind will draw in a shot of hot and humid air from the near continent, pushing UK temperatures above average.

The hottest locations in south-east England could reach 27 or 28C (82F), while England and Wales more widely will see temperatures in the mid-20s Celsius.

It comes as parts of central and southern Europe have been experiencing a spell of intense heat, with some locations exceeding 45C.

High pressure has been building in from the south where temperatures across continental Europe have been particularly high.

France and Spain have been among the hottest locations this week with temperatures exceeding 40C at times.

On Thursday, Spain saw its hottest day of 2026. Huelva in the south-west reached a staggering 45.7C.

The hottest spots in Spain will continue to exceed 40C this weekend and early next week, even around the Erbo valley in the north, which typically see temperatures closer to 20C this time of year.

Parts of southern France, including the Ardeche region, will see temperatures in the high 30s for the next few days, possibly touching 40C locally.

For the UK on Sunday, an area of low pressure will approach the north west of Scotland.

This will bring heavy rain for northern Scotland, and showers further south through the morning. It will be unseasonably blustery for western Scotland will gusts here of up to 40-45mph.

However, the wind will turn more southerly and this will scoop up the hot, humid air from the south.

The sunshine that will develop for many later in the day across England, Wales and eastern Scotland will allow temperatures to rise to unseasonable levels.

How warm will it get and how long will it last?

Across the south-east of England, central-southern England and the Welsh marches temperatures through the afternoon are likely to peak in the mid-20s Celsius quite widely.

South-west England and eastern Wales could hit 25C, while northern England will sit around the low 20s Celsius.

For eastern areas of Northern Ireland and around the Moray Firth in eastern Scotland, afternoon highs could peak at around 21 or 22C.

Average temperatures in early September are between 15 and 21C from north to south.

The warmth will be short-lived. As high pressure moves away to the east, the area of low pressure will drive more weather fronts across the UK.

By Monday, it will be even windier for north-west Scotland with coastal gales possible.

Showery outbreaks of rain will push west to east and, behind this cold front, temperatures will be lower by Tuesday.

Wednesday is forecast to be more settled with another brief ridge of high pressure but it will be cooler.

articles.title: ‘Something much bigger’: Trump planning major Middle East 'reset' after Iran war
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump is working on “something much bigger” for the Middle East once the Iran war ends, Axios reported, citing two US officials an.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump is working on “something much bigger” for the Middle East once the Iran war ends, Axios reported, citing two US officials and other sources.According to the report, the initiative is part of a broader post-Iran war strategy being developed by the Trump administration. The plan seeks to contain Tehran’s regional influence while expanding efforts to normalise relations between Israel and its neighbours.The strategy remains in the early stages of drafting and is intended to shape Washington’s approach to the Middle East both after the Iran war and during the final two years of Trump’s second and final term in office.“In recent weeks, the President has held two meetings with senior advisers to discuss the plan and raise ideas. In private conversations, he has said he is working on ‘something much bigger’ in the Middle East after the war with Iran,” two US officials said."The initial work on the strategy is being carried out both at the senior political level of the Trump administration and at the working level across various government agencies," they added.The strategyAccording to Axios, three main elements have been proposed as possible components of the strategy:Regional alignment: Building an alliance among US allies in the Gulf to contain Iran, with Washington serving as a guarantor.Addressing the October 7 fallout: Bringing the regional consequences of the October 7, 2023, attacks closer to a conclusion by securing the next phase of Trump’s Gaza plan, reaching a security agreement between Israel and Syria, and implementing the Israel-Lebanon agreement.Expanding normalisation: Broadening the Abraham Accords and pursuing a normalisation agreement between Saudi Arabia and Israel.However, officials say two major events could affect the planning: Israel’s Knesset election in October and the US midterm elections in November. Of the two, the Israeli election is viewed as the more significant, particularly as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is currently projected to lose.Trump to push his post-war plan regardless of Israel election results?However, some US officials stressed that Trump would seek to implement his post-war strategy regardless of the outcome of Israel’s election, even if it results in a political stalemate.A source briefed on the process said it could take “another few weeks” to finalise the strategy.“They are cooking it, but it is not yet cooked. The idea is to tie a whole lot of things in the region together — how you create a regional alignment after the war. It is still unclear if all US allies in the region will be on board,” the source said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
